## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dukkhāhārakathā* (Kv 2.6) is the sixth discourse of the second chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, an Abhidhamma treatise preserved in the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. The debate centers on the thesis that "sorrow as sustenance" or suffering as an intake (*dukkhāhāra*) constitutes a factor of the Path (*magganga*) and is comprised within the Path (*maggapariyāpanna*) [Bareau 1955]. The refutation demonstrates that if such an intake of suffering were indeed a path-factor, then anyone uttering the exclamation "O suffering!" (*dukkhanti*), including ordinary worldlings (*puthujjana*), matricides, parricides, murderers of arahants, and those who cause the shedding of a Buddha's blood, would thereby be developing the Path [Bareau 1955].

SuttaCentral registers no external parallels for the text, though one modern translation in one language is recorded [SuttaCentral]. In automated text-reuse analysis, DharmaNexus identifies internal textual parallels within the *Kathāvatthu* itself, sharing phrasing with the *Vohārakathā* (Kv 2.10, particularly between §1.2–2.10 and §14.2–15.10) and the *Brahmacariyakathā* (Kv 1.3) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also suggests cross-linguistic machine alignments with passages in the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D0001), though these reflect uncurated model alignments rather than established canonical parallels [DharmaNexus].
